description: plugin/typescope.lua entry, lua/typescope/{init,config,health}.lua. Verify with :checkhealth typescope.
notes:
- vim.validate avoided entirely: arg-form is 0.11+, table-form deprecated in 0.11; custom check() helper in config.lua works on both
- config.get() lazy-initializes defaults so setup() is optional (lazy.nvim friendly)
- plugin/typescope.lua is a thin shim: only registers :TypeScope, requires nothing at startup
- health: basedpyright missing is warn not error (plugin loads fine without it); Ollama checks gated on ollama.enabled
- verified headless: config validation, :checkhealth, command dispatch

title: Phase 6: LLM examples — Ollama, spinner, fallback
Phase 1: Visual spike — model, styles, highlights, render, minimal float, :TypeScope spike
description: Fixture trees cycled with <Tab>, styles with s. Validate dark/light, nerd-font fallback, wrap at max_width=40. Exit: user picks default style.
notes:
- render.lua is pure (no window APIs): returns lines/highlights/line_to_node; spike + future tests share it
- Line builder tracks byte offsets (extmarks) separately from display width (wrapping) — chrome chars are multibyte
- Wrap: hanging indent to annotation column, continuation lines carry tree bars; find_break_point() is a hard-cut placeholder awaiting smarter heuristic (TODO in render.lua)
- Gotcha: nvim_win_close fires WinClosed SYNCHRONOUSLY — redraw must detach state handles before closing old floats or the teardown autocmd nukes state mid-draw
- All charsets plain Unicode/ASCII, no nerd-font glyphs required
- Spike keymaps: <Tab> fixture, s style, e examples, b background, q close
- Remaining before close: user runs :TypeScope spike, picks default style
